intervals.label: construction and commissioning (first phase)
intervals.note: Review: first phase 1988-1993 with proposal approval, construction and installation, commissioning in 1990 and the first successful S-Au run in 1992; the status "construction" covers 1988 to the first physics run (1992).
intervals.quote: First phase (1988-1993, spokesperson Hans Specht): submission and approval of the proposal, construction and installation of the spectrometer, commissioning in 1990 with the challenging spark breakdown of the UV detectors with a S beam and the first successful S-Au run in 1992.

intervals.label: data taking (S-Au 1992, p-A 1993, Pb-Au 1995-2000)
intervals.note: Year precision: first successful S-Au run in 1992; Pb-Au data in 1995, 1996, 1999 and 2000 (last).

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event: the last data taking was Pb-Au at 158A GeV in 2000; the review also says the last CERES paper appeared in 2024.

placements.quote: CERES pioneered the measurement of electron-positron pairs at the SPS.

summary.plain: A set of ring-imaging Cherenkov counters and silicon trackers placed behind the target to pick out rare electron-positron pairs among overwhelming backgrounds, later upgraded with a radial-drift chamber.
summary.technical: CERES: two RICH detectors in a field-free region downstream of a segmented target, silicon drift chambers and (from 1999) a radial drift TPC with a magnetic field, for low-mass e+e- pair detection.

technology.value: Two ring-imaging Cherenkov detectors with silicon drift tracking (later a radial-drift TPC) for electron-pair detection
